entities.summary:
Diego Colombos (1451-11-09, Genoa) was a notorious Genoese pirate and outlaw of the Medieval period, active during the height of the Renaissance. Known for his involvement in the privateering activities of the Genoese Republic, Colombos was involved in a number of high-profile maritime disputes with the Republic of Venice.

His exploits were documented by the Venetian historian Francesco da Mosto, who noted Colombos' participation in a number of ship-to-ship battles against Venetian vessels.

The exact circumstances of Colombos' death on February 25, 1515, remain unclear, with some accounts suggesting he was killed in battle, while others claim he died of natural causes.

Despite the lack of definitive information, Colombos' legacy as a symbol of piracy and privateering during the Renaissance has endured, with his name becoming synonymous with swashbuckling adventure and daring exploits on the high seas.
